newsitem.title: USA: U.S. abortion clinic killer's convictions wiped out.
newsitem.headline: U.S. abortion clinic killer's convictions wiped out.

text.p: John Salvi, who committed suicide in prison after being convicted of killing two abortion-clinic workers, has had his convictions posthumously overturned.

Norfolk County Judge Barbara Dortch-Okara, who presided at Salvi's trial and sentenced him to life in prison, quietly voided the convictions on Jan. 21 at the request of Salvi's appellate attorney, James Sultan.

She based her ruling on a little used 25-year-old precedent by Massachusetts' highest court, the Supreme Judicial Court, which held if a defendant dies before an appeal is complete, the charges are dismissed.
Salvi, 24, committed suicide in his prison cell Nov. 29.

Defence lawyers never disputed the facts of the shootings, but argued Salvi should be found insane for wounding three people and killing two others, Lee Ann Nichols, 38, and Shannon Lowney, 25, in the December 1994 attacks.
Salvi was arrested in Virginia where police said he shot up the outside of an abortion clinic in Norfolk.
Nichols' mother, Ruth, was outraged by the judge's ruling.
"That piece of paper wipes his slate clean," she said of the judge's order, the Boston Globe reported Saturday.

"I have a piece of paper that tells me she had to have an autopsy after he pumped 10 bullets into her," the Globe quoted Ruth Nichols as saying. "They had to take her body apart. I can't wipe her autopsy clean. It's there. And so should his conviction be there."
